correctness.rationale: The published Apéry minimization follows for each nonzero residue; four-squares bounds height by four, excluding shifts of index >=3. Outside a translated union of two-square values (Landau--Ramanujan O(a/sqrt(log a))) and perfect squares (O(sqrt a)), the height is exactly 3 plus the indicator of 4^v(8u+7). Counting this unique obstruction decomposition gives a/6+O(log a) elements, hence genus 19a/6 with stated error. A terminal interval of C a/sqrt(log a) contains more obstruction residues than total bad residues, yielding conductor 4a+O(a/sqrt(log a)) and ratio 19/24 with O(1/sqrt(log a)). Independent finite shortest paths agree for 111 parameters and 12,875 residues; no extrapolation from finite samples is used. Bounds rely on the classical Landau theorem.

value.rationale: The genus, conductor and their ratio are natural core invariants. A complete limiting classification of Apéry heights for the infinite shifted-square family explains the 19/6 and 19/24 constants via the 1/6 density of three-square obstructions and sparse translated two-square exceptions. It is a parameter-uniform, quantitatively controlled global theorem rather than arbitrary finite data or a mere renaming of a Frobenius formula. No paper-sized novelty, sharp second-order term or external audit is claimed.
